You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Observed rule
The grid contains several disconnected monochrome objects. Preserve each object's shape, color, and columns (no rotation or horizontal movement). Objects that are closed frames/rings (they enclose zero cells) move vertically upward as far as possible. Objects without an enclosed hole (plus/cross-like, including asymmetric crosses) move vertically downward as far as possible. Objects stop when they hit the grid edge or another object; keep objects non-overlapping and their vertical order where their horizontal spans overlap. Output otherwise blank (0).

## Evidence
- Demo 2: hollow 3x3 color-1 frame at columns 4-6 moved from rows 2-4 to rows 0-2; hollow color-2 frame at columns 10-12 moved from rows 9-11 to rows 0-2; hollow color-5 frame at columns 2-5 moved up only to rows 3-5 because it then touched the color-1 frame whose columns overlap. Plus-like objects (colors 1, 2, 8) moved to the bottom; overlapping bottom objects stacked while preserving order.
- Test for this task was accepted with same rule. Hollow frames at columns 3-5 and 10-14 ended at the top; plus-like shapes at columns 0-2 and 10-14 settled at bottom, stacking by vertical order where spans overlapped.
- Demo 1 likewise showed hollow frames moving up and non-enclosing cross/plus objects moving down.

When a related ARC instance appears, first identify 4-connected colored components, detect whether the component encloses background cells, then vertically compact each component toward the corresponding edge without changing its shape.
